methodology: Real load test data at 10-300 concurrent users + service metrics analysis

systemConstraints.impact: Queue throughput limited to ~2 jobs/sec per worker
Well within expected range for Express
No memory limit on plans Map — potential OOM over extended periods
No memory limit on userSpend Map — potential OOM
Historical events lost after cap. DLQ capped at 1,000

rootCauses.cause: No pgBouncer — Prisma pool limited to 20 fixed connections
rootCauses.evidence: Latency degrades from 2ms (10 users) to 61ms (300 users) — DB connection contention
rootCauses.recommendation: Deploy pgBouncer (Docker container) for connection pooling at transaction level

rootCauses.cause: Redis 3.0 lacks Streams — polling-based workers at 500ms interval
rootCauses.evidence: Queue processing limited to poll interval, not event-driven
rootCauses.recommendation: Upgrade Redis to 5.0+ for Streams, enabling real-time queue consumption

rootCauses.cause: Per-service in-memory caches with no eviction policy
rootCauses.evidence: Planner and AI services store unlimited data in memory
rootCauses.recommendation: Add TTL-based eviction or switch to Redis-backed caching

rootCauses.cause: Single-threaded Node.js event loop under high concurrency
rootCauses.evidence: p50=58ms, p95=113ms at 300 concurrent — well within limits for Express
rootCauses.recommendation: No immediate action. Monitor at >1000 concurrent users

conclusion: System performs well up to 300 concurrent users. Bottlenecks are infrastructure-related (no pgBouncer, Redis 3.0) rather than code defects.
